finding_dispositions.note: Rabanus (PL 107 OCR, Mt 5:3-12 at about 91690-92200, Mt 11:28 at 101134-101140, his gifts-and-beatitudes passage at column 916) and Hilary In Matth. XI n. 15 (PL 9 OCR 77911-77920) were read at the line and checked against page images of the IA scans (the crops are in the receipts). scope.md 3.0, 3.6 and 3.7 record what each says and infers. Section 6 item 8 sets their Law-burden reading of Mt 11:28 beside Chrysostom's, and the false negatives in 3.0 and 7 are corrected. interpretations.md now names Rabanus as a carrying author of reading B, and its section 6 sentence is rewritten. The five pl107-rabanus-negative-search bindings (89-93) are replaced with reading records: 89 is the PL 107 OCR loci, 90 the PL 107 scan, 91 the PL 9 scan, and 92 the Aquinas I-II q107 a4 locus. The PL 9 OCR binding gains column 984. The PL 107 lines 93919-93920 that the study quotes as Rabanus are Augustine De serm. Dom. II.11.38 taken over by Rabanus (scope.md 3.7 and section 10).

Every multi-word literal query from sections 3.0, 3.1 and 3.8 was replayed with \s+-tolerant matching over the tracked text artifacts, and section 7 records the corrected counts. Every hit that is not a missal or a Bible text was read at the line and given a role in the bindings: a context binding with a non-commentary role, or a reading binding. PL 78 Ménard's Gregorian Sacramentary Mass (11147-11209, with the 1962 Postcommunion as its Alia) and Ménard's note (52226-52229) are now in 3.1, 3.3 and the interpretations' Collect entry and caution as the older Roman reading intercessionibus. The PL 78 Antiphonary and the PL 151 Monte Suavicino sacramentary and chant feed the malitiae history in 3.8, alongside Parma vol. 14 line 31719. The new witnesses are Bruno of Würzburg (PL 142), Gregory's Moralia I n. 24, and Augustine's Sermons XIX-XXI. The long-s diagnoses are replaced by the double-spacing cause.

In scope.md 3.8, 7 and 11, in interpretations.md, and in the binding context (binding 12), the witness is now described as its artifact record dates it: a 1951-1954 printing of the 1920 typical text with an appendix of 1970 or later. The upper bound for the alleluia's entry now rests on Mame 1922 (iuxta typicam), and the text says the 1920 typical edition itself was not read.

notes: Receipts for the source-registration stage are in .scratch/f02r/work/research-0002/. replay.py and replay.json hold the whitespace-tolerant replay of every recorded query. nonlit-hits.txt and nonlit-ids.json hold the non-missal, non-Bible hits and their artifact IDs. replay31.py, replay31b.py, win.py, win2.py, ids.py and dump.py are the line-window readers. The page images are c402r-402.png, c403l-403.png, c462r-462.png and c463l-463.png for PL 107 Rabanus, h506r-506.png for PL 9 Hilary, and g415-415.png. p401-406.html, p414-415.html, p462-463.html, q506.html and q507.html are IA page-text fetches. pl107.pdf (60,617,436 B, sha256 249f17953254e0d7a2e407129e68fea07293cebe272662c64ebd5c9d29c708d2) and pl9.pdf (80,742,141 B, sha256 eab6d2f448b2087b2f4919e7fb5ef53a77c21214d4bf0c669ea132c495867c0a) are the IA scans already registered as artifacts and verified to their fingerprints. mr1920.txt is the remote 1920-registered text layer, fetched whole and matched to its registered SHA-256. The tool receipts are validate.txt (tools/source-library validate, exit 0), check.txt (research-phase gate, exit 0) and check-disp.txt (exit 1 with --require-source-dispositions, sources[12] binding_sha256 stale, as expected). research/source-bindings.toml now has 121 bindings. research/source-dispositions.toml (112 rows, owned by the next stage and not edited here) needs a whole-file reconciliation. Intended rows are as follows. (1) Fix missale-1920-offertory-wording (binding 12) so its reason says this is a 1951-1954 printing of the 1920 typical text, not a typical-edition printing. (2) Replace the pl107-rabanus-negative-search-* rows (89-93) with deferred rows that state concrete missing criteria: Rabanus Mt 5:3-12, Mt 11:28 and the gifts passage (bindings 89-90, OCR checked against the page images, no critical edition held); Hilary In Matth. XI n. 15 (PL 9 OCR binding and binding 91); Aquinas I-II q107 a4 (binding 92). (3) Add deferred rows for the widened Augustine De serm. Dom. loci (from line 932) and Sermons XIX-XXI, for Gregory's Moralia I n. 24, for the PL 78 Sacramentary, Antiphonary and Ménard note, for the PL 151 sacramentary and chant, for Parma vol. 14 line 31719, and for Bruno of Würzburg in PL 142. (4) Give the roughly 29 new replay-hit context bindings (93 onward) non-commentary-use or not-author rows. (5) Re-hash every binding whose context changed: 12, the Durandus/Beleth binding, the NPNF I.6, PL 9 OCR, Moralia, Guéranger vol. 15, Sarum, PL 78, PL 151, PL 142, PL 202 and Parma bindings. Defects for other owners (scope.md section 10): tools/source-library search has no whitespace-tolerant mode and gives no double-spacing warning, and negative-search bindings carry no check against it; the PL artifact notes lack the spacing warning and the loci; PL 151 and PL 142 filing; author-standing-v1.toml has no row for Bruno of Würzburg; the lane comment and carrying_authors in proper-components.toml omit Rabanus from reading B; the study sections (sections/30-beatitudes-way-of-the-saints.tex lines 54-58, sections/90-apparatus.tex) quote PL 107 lines 93919-93920 as Rabanus's own words, but the passage is Augustine De serm. Dom. II.11.38 taken over by Rabanus, and the sections still describe the 1920 witness, the intercessionibus reading and the malitiae history in the superseded way.
summary: This dispatch read and recorded the held Rabanus and Hilary commentaries on Mt 5 and Mt 11:28 (with their Law-burden reading set beside Chrysostom), replayed every recorded multi-word search with whitespace-tolerant matching and dispositioned the new non-missal hits (PL 78 Gregorian Sacramentary and Ménard's intercessionibus note, PL 78 and PL 151 chant books, Parma vol. 14, Bruno of Würzburg, Gregory's Moralia, Aquinas I-II q107, Augustine's Sermons XIX-XXI), redated the misnamed 1920 Missal witness, and bound every locus read.
